correctness.rationale: On the cone over K_{m,m} minus a perfect matching, average over simultaneous index permutations and side swaps. A hub edge weight a has 2ma<=1, and the periphery has diagonal 1-a-(m-1)b. The hub contrast has eigenvalue 1-(2m+1)a. On the side contrast and the two zero-sum standard spaces, use the cross block b(11^T-I) to get v=1-a-2(m-1)b, u=1-a-(m-2)b for antisymmetric vectors, and 1-a-mb for symmetric vectors. The identity 2(m-1)u-(m-2)v=m(1-a) bounds SLEM below by t=(2m-1)/(2(3m-4)). Equality forces a=1/(2m), u=t, v=-t. The resulting b=2t/m gives positive peripheral holding, zero hub holding, and remaining nontrivial eigenvalues -1/(2m) and (m-4)t/m of modulus at most t for m>=4. For any optimizer, the averaged kernel is this invariant matrix. The PSD constraints tI-P_g and tI+P_g on 1-perp force every conjugated kernel to agree on the active +t and -t eigenspaces: a PSD quadratic form that vanishes on a vector annihilates it. Time reversal here is matrix symmetry, not an invariance assumption on the optimizer. The +t antisymmetric zero-sum space forces each row and each column of the allowed cross weights to be constant, since the corresponding coefficient vector is orthogonal to the zero-sum space. Distinct rows have a common allowed column, making every cross weight equal; both sides then have a common hub weight. The -t side contrast gives the second equality a+2(m-1)b=1+t and fixes those weights, and row sums fix all diagonals. This certifies uniqueness without assuming graph invariance of P and gives the limit 1/3 directly.
residual_risks: The bounded check is corroboration only; the PSD rigidity and support calculation establish the universal claim. No inference about nonsymmetric kernels or other mixing criteria.

checked_sources: Boyd et al., Graphs with Symmetries, Theorem 2.1
value.rationale: Crown cones naturally combine a hub and a sparsified bipartite core. Their exact optimum makes the two active eigenvalue constraints explicit. The rigidity proof answers a question symmetry reduction leaves open: whether a nonsymmetric assignment of edge weights under graph automorphisms can match the optimal SLEM. This is a structural result for an infinite family, rather than just evaluating a solver or repeating a transfer formula.
residual_risks: The scope is exact SLEM optimality in one uniform-stationary family, not a general stability theorem or an optimization of finite-time mixing distance.
